overrideReason: All 3 attempts were rejected purely on C7, a [browser:] criterion requiring a real screenshot of the frozen badge rendering on the live board — structurally something no codex/claude sandbox can produce (same class as PRD-009's US-908 sparkline screenshots). While attempt 3 was still running, I independently investigated why the story's own capture-frozen-badge.mjs script (present since attempt 1) failed to find the badge: a debug browser session against the mixed-board fixture showed BTC MVRV rendering as plain 'OK 4.11' with no frozen badge at all, despite the fixture correctly declaring it frozen. I traced buildBoard's integrityRows matching, CellFace.tsx's frozen-badge rendering, and CellDetail.tsx's wiring, and everything looked structurally correct on paper - but caught myself investigating live files that attempt 3's codex process was concurrently editing (mixedBoard.ts, FrozenBadge.test.tsx), so I stopped and discarded that investigation rather than trust a moving target. Attempt 3 finished, was rejected on the same C7, but had genuinely fixed the real wiring bug in the process (it touched exactly the files my aborted investigation suspected). I re-ran the story's own capture-frozen-badge.mjs script myself on the final, stable, committed state - it succeeded cleanly. I visually reviewed both resulting screenshots: the cell shows 'unchanged since 10 Sep 2026' as plain grey text, the OK status dot and colour are completely unchanged, and the expanded detail panel shows 'Integrity: Frozen value unchanged since 10 Sep 2026, 00:00:00 UTC' as additive information only - no colour-coding, no severity tiering, exactly matching the story's own prohibition on reintroducing judgement. Re-ran the full offline suite after: uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" (504 passed), npm --prefix web run typecheck (clean), npm --prefix web test (78/78, including FrozenBadge.test.tsx's four real test cases matching C1-C4 by name).
